sources.scope: General principles for presenting dimensions and associated tolerances
Dimensioning, tolerancing and GD&T design language
Import model annotations into selected drawing views and suppress duplicates
Create a native drawing section view from selected section-line sketch segments
Create a native drawing detail boundary and scaled detail view
Selection marks and parameters for native feature linear patterns
Native circular pattern instance count, angle, equal spacing and selection marks
Native feature mirror selection marks and side-effect controls
Linear, ordinate, radial and angular dimensions plus center marks and centerlines
Named styles controlling arrows, text, units and tolerances

rules.rule: Dimension and tolerance plans must express function, manufacture and inspection intent; no tolerance is invented when absent.
Place a feature dimension in the view where the feature has the clearest true shape; add section or detail views only when required for unambiguous definition.
First-angle or third-angle projection must come from the user or project template and must be recorded in the drawing plan.
Define each required size once, then define feature locations from functional datums or stable reference edges; avoid duplicate and contradictory dimensions.
Use diameter callouts for complete circles and holes, radius callouts for arcs and fillets, and add center marks or centerlines for circular features and axes.
A hole plan separates size, type, depth or through condition, count and location; threaded, counterbored and countersunk holes require dedicated callouts.
Repeated features use count plus spacing, pitch-circle or ordinate/baseline location logic instead of a redundant dimension on every instance.
Prefer dimensions outside view geometry, group related dimensions, keep consistent offsets and move text or dimension lines when crossings or collisions are detected.
Compute a usable sheet zone from sheet boundaries and title-block reservation before scaling and placing views or annotations.
Prefer native associative model annotations and native AutoCAD dimension objects so updates propagate with geometry changes.
Keep document identity, title, material, scale, revision and approval data as structured title-block fields; report conflicts instead of choosing silently.
A drawing passes only when required views and annotations exist, geometry stays inside the usable sheet zone, outputs are non-empty and no unresolved conflicts remain.
